description:
How a person's, company's or entity's podcast mentions are moving, for tracking it week over week. Two modes:
  - `compare` (default): which podcasts mentioned it in a window (default the last 7 days, at most 90) and how each compares with the equal-length window before it: episode and mention line counts in both, the delta, and a label. A show in both windows is `continuing`; one only in the previous is `dropped`. A show only in the current window is judged against the lookback before it (`lookback_days`, default 90): `new` when it never mentioned the subject there, published at least four episodes there, and has two or more mention lines now; `returning` when it mentioned the subject earlier in the lookback; `passing` for a single line; `newly_tracked` when it published too little in the lookback to tell. Totals for both windows count every podcast. Filter with `change`, order with `sort` (`rising` and `falling` for the biggest movers), and page with `cursor`. Answers "which shows talked about Nike this week versus last?" in one call, and, with `change="new"` (sorted by popularity unless `sort` is set), "which podcasts started talking about Nike this month?" or "which mentioned Nike for the first time?": read what the leading shows said with `particle_podcast_find_mentions`. Since 2026-10-23, `new` no longer means every show absent from the previous window; that set is now `new`, `returning`, `passing` and `newly_tracked` together.
  - `timeseries`: mention counts per day, week or month over a range (omit `published_after` for all time), each bucket with its episodes, mention lines and distinct podcasts. Answers "is it rising?". `podcast_slug` charts one show.

Mentions inside ad reads are left out unless `include_ads`, so a brand that advertises heavily is measured by what shows say about it. The newest day fills in over about a day as episodes are processed, so a window ending now reads slightly low and the current bucket is marked partial: compare full buckets.

Podcast slugs in the response work with `particle_podcast_find_mentions` (with the same dates as `since` and `until`, to read what a show said) and `particle_podcast_list_episodes`. Not for the mention lines themselves (`particle_podcast_find_mentions`), appearance or topic trends by role or keyword (`particle_podcast_get_episode_timeseries`, which counts an episode for a company named only in its ad reads), or a split by who said it (`particle_podcast_get_share_of_voice`). To be told about new mentions as they air, create an alert with `particle_alert_create`.

change.description: compare only: keep podcasts with this label. 'new': started talking about the subject: two or more mention lines in the window, none in the lookback before it, on a show that published at least four episodes there. Use it for 'which shows started talking about X' or 'mentioned X for the first time'. 'returning': back after a gap in the lookback. 'passing': a single line, a first in the lookback. 'newly_tracked': too little published history to tell (fewer than four episodes in the lookback, which includes a monthly show over the default 90 days: pass lookback_days=180 for those). 'continuing': both windows. 'dropped': the previous window only.

company_slug.description: Company slug or domain from particle_company_resolve (e.g. 'nvidia'). Resolves to the company's linked entity.

cursor.description: compare only: cursor from a previous response. Pass published_after and published_before as that response's window so the page lines up.

entity_slug.description: Knowledge-graph entity slug from particle_entity_resolve for anything that isn't a person or company (e.g. 'germany').

guest_capacity.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest who knows their field in this capacity (e.g. 'public_official' for politicians). particle_expertise_resolve names the capacity an everyday word means.

guest_field.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest listed under this ANZSRC 2020 field of research: a code, slug or title from particle_expertise_resolve.

guest_in_field.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest speaking within their own field (the guest the other guest_ filters select, when given).

guest_occupation.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest listed under this occupation: a SOC 2018 or ISCO-08 code, slug or title from particle_expertise_resolve, or a SOC group or everyday name (e.g. 'financial-and-investment-analysts' or 'physicians'). A word with no occupation filters by the field of research or capacity it names: 'investors' is field 350208, 'politicians' is capacity public_official.

guest_practicing.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest who still works in guest_occupation, which must be a SOC 2018 occupation or group.

guest_seniority.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest at this seniority or above.

guest_standing.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest whose standing is recognized this way: 'established' (conferred by others), 'self_described', or 'unverified'.

include_ads.description: Count mentions inside ad reads too. Off by default, so a brand that advertises heavily is measured by what shows say about it, not its own ads.

interval.description: Bucket width. timeseries: defaults to week. compare: adds each podcast's counts per bucket over the current window.

language.description: Only podcasts in this language: ISO 639-1 code (e.g. 'fr'), matched on the podcast's primary language subtag.

limit.description: compare only: podcasts per page (1-50, default 10).

lookback_days.description: compare only: days before published_after a podcast must not have mentioned the subject in to be 'new' (7-180, default 90; never shorter than the previous window).

mode.description: 'compare' (default): which podcasts mentioned the subject in the window and how each compares with the equal-length window before it, with both windows' totals. 'timeseries': mention counts per day, week or month over a range, with the podcasts carrying them per bucket.

output_format.description: Output serialization. 'markdown' (default) returns the LLM-facing rendering. 'json' returns the structured payload as JSON text — use only for programmatic chaining where exact field extraction matters; the JSON shape is larger and noisier for an LLM to read.

person_slug.description: Person slug from particle_person_resolve (e.g. 'sam-altman'). One of person_slug, company_slug or entity_slug is required.

podcast_slug.description: timeseries only: chart the mentions on one podcast (slug from particle_podcast_resolve). In compare mode the rows are the podcasts.

published_after.description: compare: start of the current window (ISO 8601 date or date-time); defaults to 7 days before published_before, and the window may span at most 90 days. timeseries: start of the range; omit to chart all time.

published_before.description: End of the current window or range: a bare date includes that whole UTC day. Defaults to now.

publisher_slug.description: Only mentions on podcasts of this publisher (network), by slug.

role.description: Constrain how the subject participates: guest, host, panelist, correspondent, or mention. In compare mode the lookback's earlier-mention check counts any mention whatever the role, so a first guest appearance on a show that named the subject before is 'returning', not 'new'.

sort.description: compare only: 'mentions' (most current-window mention lines first), 'rising' or 'falling' (largest gain or loss from the previous window first), or 'popularity' (biggest shows first). Defaults to popularity with change 'new' or 'returning', else mentions.

name: particle_podcast_get_mention_trends
title: Particle Podcast Get Mention Trends
